findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete data source for reused successful-unit CONTENT (sidecar `findings` and/or checkpoint envelopes) and the join from journal unit ids to that content, since the discovery journal itself is content-free.
evidence: sidecar.py _discovery_journal: 'The reducer-IGNORED discovery execution journal: the safe (content-free) per-unit Pass-1 trace records'
pass1.py _trace_record: 'Build the SAFE (content-free) discovery-journal record for one unit outcome'
Actual finding content is persisted in sidecar.build_payload `findings` (_slim) and in CheckpointEnvelope.content, not in the discovery journal
Plan says retry reuses 'clean and blocking results' from the journal but the journal carries no results content
findings.finding: The plan sources reused successful-unit results from 'the latest completed versioned RP-06 review journal', but the existing discovery journal is content-free and reducer-ignored (it stores per-unit outcomes, not finding content); the actual reusable content lives in the sidecar findings list and/or the chunk checkpoints. The plan never specifies the data source or the join used to reconstruct each reused unit's actual result, leaving the reuse/recombine data-flow underspecified.
findings.location: Approach — 'reads the latest completed versioned RP-06 review journal' / 'Reuse every eligible successful unit'
scenarios: An eligible retry must recombine two successful units' findings with one newly-recovered unit, but the journal it reads has no finding content to reuse
Implementer wires retry to the content-free journal and silently loses the reused findings, or improvises an unspecified sidecar/checkpoint join
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that retry reconstructs reused units from the persisted sidecar `findings` (and/or reusable checkpoint envelopes) keyed by the journal's per-unit ids, and that the content-free discovery journal is used only to identify which units succeeded vs. are missing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the 'stale' refusal condition concretely (e.g., journal schema/codec-version older than current, or an explicit freshness/version predicate) distinct from digest-mismatch, so eligibility is deterministically computable.
evidence: 'stale' appears as a refusal trigger separately from 'digest-mismatched', implying a non-content dimension of eligibility that is never specified
Signal (2) implicit acceptance criteria: an executor cannot deterministically compute 'stale' without a stated definition
findings.finding: The refusal condition 'stale' is listed alongside 'digest-mismatched' as a distinct ineligibility trigger, but the plan never defines what makes a journal stale (a time bound? a schema/version bound? something orthogonal to digest content-identity?).
findings.location: Approach: 'Fail before any model call when the latest result is ... stale, corrupt, legacy, or digest-mismatched'; AC4: 'stale ... journal refuses before any model/provider call'
scenarios: An executor must decide whether a syntactically-valid, digest-matching journal is nonetheless 'stale' and cannot determine the rule
findings.suggested_fix: State the staleness rule explicitly, e.g. 'stale = the journal was written by an older journal-codec/schema version than the current reader supports' and note it is orthogonal to the digest-identity check.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the retry reader against the existing chunk-atomic checkpoint system (sizing.checkpoint_identity/load_checkpoint + pass1.run_pass1): state explicitly whether the new journal reader REUSES that lineage-digest/eligibility machinery or why a separate implementation is required.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:711 checkpoint_identity binds material + criterion set + model/mode + extra-context + policy_digest + code_ref + topology_digest into the envelope identity digest

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:742 load_checkpoint 'any read/parse error, corrupt JSON, legacy namespace, a digest mismatch, or a non-reusable kind ⇒ None (re-run the chunk)' — the same eligibility/refusal semantics the plan re-specifies

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:337-360 run_pass1 resumes cached SUCCESS chunks (resumed+=1) and executes only the un-cached (missing) chunks — i.e. reuse-successes/re-run-missing already exists per run
findings.finding: The plan's new 'versioned RP-06 review journal' retry reader — reuse eligible successful units, re-run only missing units, gated on a digest-complete lineage over material/code-ref/policy/prompts/model-mode/topology/context — closely duplicates the existing production chunk-atomic checkpoint/resume system (sizing.checkpoint_identity / load_checkpoint / save_checkpoint driven from pass1.run_pass1), which already reuses completed SUCCESS units, re-runs the rest, keys the same lineage axes, and rejects corrupt/legacy/digest-mismatched envelopes. The plan neither cites this layer nor says whether the retry reader extends it or rebuilds its lineage-digest/eligibility machinery.
findings.location: Approach — 'reads the latest completed versioned RP-06 review journal … lineage must be digest-complete and content-identical across ticket material, code/ref, effective policy, prompts/contracts, model/mode, topology, context, dependencies, and source'
scenarios: An implementer builds a second lineage-digest + eligibility path in the retry reader when load_checkpoint already provides one, doubling the surface that must stay consistent with the review's identity axes
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Approach note reconciling the retry path with sizing.load_checkpoint: e.g. reuse checkpoint_identity for the lineage digest and load_checkpoint's corrupt/legacy/digest-mismatch refusals, so the retry reader only adds the 'latest-INDETERMINATE-eligibility + fresh-attempt-budget' semantics on top rather than re-deriving digest completeness and content-identity.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the positive rationale for a new journal-based retry reader versus extending the existing digest-guarded chunk-checkpoint resume, and how the two lineage-identity definitions relate (or are shared).
evidence: sizing.checkpoint_identity binds 'material, criterion set, model/mode, injected extra-context, or policy/code/topology refs' — nearly the same lineage list the plan's digest-completeness requires
pass1._chunk already resumes completed chunks via load_checkpoint and re-runs missing ones (coverage['checkpoint'] = {chunks_resumed, chunks_total})

Plan's Context justifies retry-over-full-rerun and warns against 'blindly resuming old checkpoints' (a valid rejection of BLIND resume) but does not justify a NEW journal reader over a checkpoint resume gated by the same digest-completeness check
findings.finding: A structurally-similar resume mechanism already exists — the chunk-atomic checkpoint system (sizing.load_checkpoint/save_checkpoint + pass1 resume) keyed by a digest binding material, criteria set, model/mode, extra-context, and policy/code/topology, which already implements 'reuse completed units, re-run missing ones'. The plan builds a parallel journal-based retry reader and dismisses the checkpoint layer only as 'legacy checkpoints never seed retry' without a positive rationale for why a new reader is preferable to extending the existing digest-guarded checkpoint resume with the same content-identity guard.
findings.location: Approach — 'a narrow library-internal retry request that reads the latest completed versioned RP-06 review journal' and 'Legacy REVIEW_RESULT payloads and legacy checkpoints never seed retry'
scenarios: Reviewer/maintainer asks why two overlapping resume mechanisms exist
Implementer duplicates checkpoint-identity logic in the journal reader, risking divergence between the two lineage-identity definitions
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence explaining why the versioned journal (durable, digest-complete, sidecar-backed) is the correct retry seed rather than the git-ignored best-effort checkpoint cache — e.g. checkpoints are per-chunk optimization caches without a persisted whole-review verdict/eligibility record — and note whether checkpoint-identity logic is reused to avoid two divergent lineage checks.

Plan text: 'Add CLI parsing and a narrow library-internal retry request'; '--retry is mutually exclusive with --force, --status, and --check' — all framed as CLI flags
The plan enumerates CLI + docs edit targets but does not mention the MCP review_plan surface as either in- or out-of-scope

scenarios: An operator or maintainer expects retry to be reachable via the MCP review_plan tool the same way force is, or conversely assumes it was updated when it was intentionally left CLI-only

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'a normal rerun repeats everything' premise with the existing checkpoint resume (pass1.run_pass1) and state precisely which behavior the retry adds that a plain re-run does not already provide.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:286-341 'Chunk-atomic CHECKPOINTING … resume completed Pass-1 chunks from a prior run' — a normal re-run already resumes cached successes rather than repeating everything
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:669 checkpoint dir '.rebar/cache/plan-review/<ticket_id>' persists across runs
findings.finding: The plan's stated problem — 'A normal rerun repeats everything' — appears contradicted by the existing checkpoint resume, which already reuses completed successful Pass-1 units across runs when the lineage digest is unchanged. If a plain re-run already resumes successful units, the plan should state what the retry adds beyond the fresh-attempt-budget grant, otherwise the motivating premise (and the reuse portion of the value) is weaker than claimed.
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'A normal rerun repeats everything, while blindly resuming old checkpoints risks applying results to changed material or policy'
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer over-scopes the retry feature to deliver reuse that the checkpoint layer already provides, when the only novel behavior needed is the fresh attempt-budget grant and latest-review eligibility gate

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the retry eligibility/lineage check reuses the reuse.py material/code-SHA baseline comparison shared by idempotent_reuse and verdict_reuse, or justify a distinct comparison for the INDETERMINATE case.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:53 idempotent_reuse — PASS reuse gated by claim_gate_check (material fingerprint + code SHA + registry stamp)
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:121 verdict_reuse — BLOCK reuse gated by material_fingerprint + verified_at_sha, mirroring remediation_mode._sidecar_branch_decision
Plan restricts retry to the INDETERMINATE latest verdict, the one case the two existing reuse siblings deliberately do NOT cover
findings.finding: The lineage/content-identity + latest-verdict eligibility check the retry adds is a third instance of an already-established pattern: reuse.idempotent_reuse (PASS) and reuse.verdict_reuse (BLOCK) both read the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar and gate reuse on material_fingerprint + verified_at_sha (and ticket-type). The plan should confirm the retry eligibility check extends/mirrors these sibling reuse gates rather than introducing an unrelated fourth verdict-reuse path.
findings.location: Approach — 'Eligibility requires that exact latest review to be INDETERMINATE with retryable missing calls. The lineage must be digest-complete and content-identical …'
scenarios: An implementer writes a bespoke sidecar/journal freshness comparison for retry when reuse.py already centralizes the material/code-SHA baseline comparison used by the PASS and BLOCK reuse paths
